_comment: Golden values for scripts/33_rocket_mb_dronet_pext_board.sh -- DroNet at int8 on hart 0 of the P-ext bitstream (PynqZ2RocketBigLittlePextTacitConfig, MAGIC 0x5A5A0004, 34.4828 MHz), with the three MBP kernels of PEXT_KERNELS.md plus the two INTEGER kernels of DRONET_INTEGER.md standing in for batchnorm2d_s8 and add_s8. The split between exact values and ranges is the same as expected/modelblaster_lenet_int8_pext.json's and for the same reason: exact for anything structural, a window for anything measured, and nothing at all for a raw cycle count.
_bit_exactness: max_abs_err_vs_scalar_golden is the element-by-element difference between the 2-byte int8 output tensor the board produced (printed by samples/modelblaster_pext as MB_PEXT_OUT) and the baked int8 golden the SCALAR codegen emitted from the byte-identical IR. Measured [-56, 127] against [-56, 127]. It is pinned to 0 because 0 is the only acceptable value, and for DroNet it rests on one more link than LeNet's did: batchnorm2d_s8 and add_s8 run INTEGER fixed-point kernels whose general accuracy class is numeric_drift, not bit_exact. PEXT_SPEC.md section 1.5 is right that the integer rescale-add is not bit-exact in general -- over random scale triples 14.3% of them drift somewhere, always by exactly 1 LSB. integer_kernels_exhaustively_bit_exact below is the per-model proof that it does not drift HERE, and it is a proof rather than a sample: both kernels are pointwise int8 maps, so 229,376 cases is their ENTIRE input domain. Re-run it after any recalibration, because recalibration is exactly what could invalidate it. If it ever fails, the fix is to keep the float reference for the affected op -- NOT to widen this number.
_why_kernels_integer_only_is_absent: 24 and 30 compute and pin `kernels_integer_only`, a grep of the generated kernels.c for /float|double|roundf|.../. That flag is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE for DroNet and pinning it either way would be meaningless: kernel_batchnorm2d_s8's SIGNATURE is (const int8_t *input, const float *scale, const float *bias, ...), so the word `float` is in kernels.c whatever the kernel body does. Stage 6 of the runner measures the thing that grep was a proxy for instead -- which functions actually CALL libgcc soft-float, and where. Result: conv2d_s8, linear_s8, maxpool2d_s8 and relu_s8 contain none; batchnorm2d_s8 and add_s8 contain them only in per-channel and per-dispatch setup, never in an element loop; sigmoid_s8 keeps the float reference for its single element. See DRONET_INTEGER.md section 5.

_measured._comment: Not checked -- recorded so a future run has something to compare against. rdcycle at 34,482,759 Hz (read back from the PS SLCR, outside the SoC), 3 timed iterations, the other hart idle, interrupts masked per iteration. Built with the runner's default MB_PEXT_CONV_WBYTES=65536.

conv_wbytes_sweep_on_board._comment: All three bit-exact. Instructions fall 24.1% from 8192 to 65536 but cycles only 13.5%, because the repacked-weight block outgrows the 16 KB L1D. Spike cannot see the difference; the board can.

what_the_integer_kernels_bought._comment: Counterfactual from the same spike harness at the shipped 8192 block: MBP convolutions with the FLOAT reference batchnorm/add. This is the number the whole exercise was about.

_range_comment: pext_hart0_median_cycles is deliberately NOT pinned -- it moves with any compiler, Zephyr or codegen change and a red check there would say nothing about the hardware. What is pinned is a WIDE window on the frame time, whose only job is to catch the two failure modes that matter: the MBP kernels silently not being selected (which would read as ~15x this, since the scalar frame is 346 M instructions), or the image falling back to pext.h's software model (slower still). Anything inside this window is a performance change to investigate, not a correctness failure.
